findings.claim: An unrelated hunk removes the `case <= byte.MaxValue` branch from an unsigned writer in MessagePackPrimitives. Integers 128..255 are now written as uint16 (0xcd 0x00 0xNN, 3 bytes) instead of uint8 (0xcc 0xNN, 2 bytes). That changes the wire bytes of every payload containing such values, which matters for byte-compatibility, hashing and signature consumers. It also breaks the smallest-encoding contract, and REQ-2283 does not call for it.

A byte-diff of MessagePackSerializer.Serialize(200u) between base and head shows the same thing.

findings.claim: The new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper drops every diagnostic whose location is Location.None, not only those for metadata symbols. GetPropertyIdentifierLocation now returns null whenever the declaring syntax is not a PropertyDeclarationSyntax. For a positional record property in source, e.g. `record R([property: Key(null)] string X)`, the declaring syntax is a ParameterSyntax. So BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull for a source type in the compiling assembly is now silently swallowed instead of being reported (it previously threw InvalidCastException). The helper should fall back to the declaring syntax location (or the formatted type's identifier) instead of null.

findings.claim: MemberNeedsKey now passes a null location when `item` has no declaring syntax, and the wrapper then drops it. Take a source [MessagePackObject] class in the compiling assembly that derives from a base class in a referenced assembly, where the base has a public property without [Key]. The required MsgPack004 for that source type is now silently dropped, even though the formatted type itself is in source.
